_schema: Market reference data. The engine fetches live prices and FX from IBKR at build time; these values are fallbacks for --gold-aud / --euraud and the documented basis for any figure computed offline.

xau_usd.note: Range 4,370-4,440 mid-August. Up 7.76% over the month, 31.15% year on year. Recent path: 4,183.85 (5 Aug), 4,270.62 (6 Aug), 4,305.29 (7 Aug), 4,363.70 (13 Aug).

xau_aud.note: DERIVED: 4,376.07 / 0.7092. Used for Channel 2a reserve-price gaps and Channel 3 operating leverage.

history_2026.note: Record US$5,589/oz on 28 Jan 2026 on US-Iran tensions, record central bank buying (~60 t/month vs a pre-2022 average of 17 t) and record ETF inflows. Corrected to ~4,091 by mid-March, recovered to ~4,541 late March, ~4,678 on 12 May. Gold gained 64% in 2025, its best year since 1979. Central banks bought an estimated 289 t in Q2 2026; China added ~20 t in July, a 21st consecutive month.

gold.drawdown_note: The Jan-to-Mar 2026 drawdown of roughly 27% peak to trough is a live illustration of the ounce arithmetic in methodology §0.1: a linearly levered portfolio bleeds ounces through exactly this kind of round trip. Only convexity accumulates.

aud_usd.note: 7-day range 0.7055-0.7083; 30-day 0.6959-0.7083; 90-day 0.6882-0.7189. AUD firm since early August on RBA signalling.

eur_aud.note: APPROXIMATE. AUD per EUR. Fetch live from IBKR at build time — this is a fallback only.

fund.note: Simulation AUM. At this size the capacity test (position <= 5 days of median ADVT at 20% participation) is INERT — a 3% weight is ~A$49,000, a few percent of one day's volume in the smallest name screened. Spread is the entire liquidity cost, which is why Gate 3 is spread-based rather than market-cap based.
fund.capacity_note: Estimated methodology capacity before the small-cap tail begins to bind. Above roughly A$50-100m, names below ~A$1bn market cap drop progressively. The EUR1m simulation is therefore a PURER expression of the methodology than a scaled fund can run — results will not reflect capacity drag.

asx_tick_schedule.note: Gate 3 §4.1. The ASX tick regime converts a spread limit into a SHARE PRICE floor, not a size floor.
asx_tick_schedule.implication: A 1.0% producer spread limit implies a practical share-price floor near A$0.50, and A$1.00 for comfort. At A$0.10 one tick is 5.0% of price; at A$0.145 it is 3.4%; at A$0.55 it is 0.91%; at A$1.00 it is 0.50%.

binding_cases.outcome: EXCLUDED — cannot quote inside 1.0% at any volume.
Inside the 4.0% developer limit, outside the 1.0% producer limit. Moot — AAR fails Gate 2 D2 and D3 on fundamentals.

reserve_deck_cross_section.note: Channel 2a input. Reserve price assumptions against a spot of A$6,170/oz. The gap is disclosed, JORC-mandated, and invisible to any methodology reading only the headline reserve number.
reserve_deck_cross_section.observation: A 2.3x spread across the sourced cross-section. Capricorn books reserves at roughly 39% of spot; Vault books at roughly 90%. Same commodity, same country, same quarter — the difference is entirely accounting conservatism, and it is exactly the unbooked optionality Channel 2a is designed to harvest. Note GMD's figure (A$2,500-3,500) is a RESOURCE guideline, not a reserve deck, and is excluded from this table.
